_note: The FAMILY's moments (session P1, GDD 4.9.5; format in README.md). Senders: parent / parent:mum / parent:dad / parent:athlete (the one who ran) / sibling / family. The family's attitude (data/cast.json attitudes, condition `family`) decides which moments fit and which text variant is used; a reply's `attitude` effect can change it (the 'against' family comes round slowly). Topics: `card` (the evening after a report card, queued by StoryletSystem) and `app` (after the application's results). Moments never change what is trained: a reply moves moods, relationships, a late night (sleep), the grades or a remembered flag. Ages 14-16 (P2 adds 16-17). Every person is fictional.

text: Dinner was at six. It's cold now. Is it going to be like this every training day?
We waited for you with dinner again. Can you tell us when practice runs late?

text.text: You came home at eight and ate standing up. Athletes need proper meals, you know that better than anyone.

replies.label: Sorry, I'll text when I'm late
replies.result: Thank you. That's all we ask.

replies.label: Can you keep a plate warm for me?
replies.result: Fine. Microwave, second shelf.

replies.label: Practice is practice
replies.result: And dinner is dinner. We'll talk about this.

text: I have a meeting tonight, I can't drive you to practice. Can you sort it out yourself?
The car is at the garage today. How are you getting to practice?

replies.label: I'll take the bus
replies.result: Thanks. Take a warm hat.

replies.label: I'll ask {partner}'s family
replies.result: Good thinking. Say thank you from us.

replies.label: I'll cycle, it's a warm-up
replies.result: In this weather? Lights on, then.

text: Your running shoes have holes in them. How much do proper ones cost these days?
I saw your shoes in the hall. Those are finished. Do you need new ones?

replies.label: The good ones, please
replies.result: That much? All right. Look after them.

replies.label: Cheaper ones will do
replies.result: That's sensible of you. Thank you.

replies.label: They'll last a few more weeks
replies.result: Tell me when they don't.

text: We're going to see Grandma on Sunday. She asks about your running every time. Coming?
Grandpa turns 75 on Sunday. The whole family will be there. You're coming, right?

replies.label: Of course I'm coming
replies.result: They'll want to hear everything about your races.

replies.label: I'll come and run there
replies.result: Bring your shoes then. The forest road is nice there.

replies.label: I'd rather stay and train
replies.result: She won't be around forever, you know.

text: {meet} is coming up. Should we come and watch?
Can we come to {meet}? I promise not to shout too loud.

text.text: I'll be at {meet}. I want to see how you run the first lap.

replies.label: Yes, come!
replies.result: We'll be in the stands. Wave at us.

replies.label: Please don't, I get nervous
replies.result: All right. Text us the result.

replies.label: Only if you stay quiet
replies.result: Quiet as mice. Mostly.

text: We saw the result! Well done. Pizza on Friday?

text.text: {pb}! I ran faster at your age, but not by much. Proud of you.
A good race. Champions don't celebrate small steps for long, but tonight you can.
My colleagues saw it on the club's page. I told them: that's my kid. Well done!
The neighbour saw your result in the paper. So, well done, I suppose.

replies.label: Thanks! It felt good
replies.result: You've earned it.

replies.label: I can go faster
replies.result: We know you can.

replies.label: It was OK
replies.result: OK? It was better than OK.

text: I saw the result. Do you want to talk, or do you want ice cream?

text.text: What happened on the second lap? You went too early. I could see it from the stands.
One bad race. Your grandfather used to say: lose, learn, come back.
Maybe this is a sign to concentrate on school for a while?

replies.label: Let's talk
replies.result: Come to the kitchen. I'll put the kettle on.

replies.label: I want to be alone
replies.result: All right. We're here when you want.

replies.label: Just leave it
replies.result: Fine. I was only trying to help.

text: In my day we ran 10 × 400 every Tuesday, no matter what. Is your coach giving you enough speed work?
I watched your session from the fence. Your arms cross in front when you get tired. Want me to show you?
When I was your age my coach made us run the stadium stairs until we couldn't feel our legs. Different times.

replies.label: Show me
replies.result: Saturday in the yard, then. Bring your spikes.

replies.label: {coach_first} has a plan
replies.result: Of course. I'm just saying.

replies.label: Training has changed since then
replies.result: Hmph. Some things never change.

text: Your split at 400 was too slow. You can't win from that far back.
Good, but you left something in the tank. I could see it.

replies.label: You're right
replies.result: Next time, then.

replies.label: It was the plan
replies.result: Then it's your coach's plan I disagree with.

replies.label: Can I just enjoy it?
replies.result: ...Yes. You're right. Sorry.

text: Champions train when nobody is watching. Did you do your stretching today?
I made the national team because I never missed a session. Remember that.
Your room is a mess. Discipline starts at home.

replies.label: Yes, I did it all
replies.result: Good. That's the way.

replies.label: I'm doing my best
replies.result: I know. I just want it for you.

replies.label: It's a lot of pressure
replies.result: ...I didn't mean it like that. We'll ease off.

text: Is all this running going to get you anywhere? Your cousin is learning to code.
Six practices a week. What about your future?
Nobody makes a living from running around a track in Finland.

replies.label: Watch my next race
replies.result: ...Maybe. If it doesn't clash with anything.

replies.label: My grades are fine too
replies.result: They had better stay fine.

replies.label: It's my life
replies.result: Not while you live under this roof.

text: You have tests this week. Maybe skip practice until they're done?
Tests first, running later. Promise me you'll study tonight.

replies.label: I'll study tonight, I promise
replies.result: Good. I'll make you tea.

replies.label: I can do both
replies.result: We'll see the results.

replies.label: Practice isn't the problem
replies.result: We'll see who's right when the grades come.

text: I read about you in the local paper today. Your name was there. I didn't know you were that good. Why didn't you tell us?

replies.label: I tried to
replies.result: ...I know. Maybe I should come to a race.

replies.label: Come to my next race
replies.result: All right. Tell me when.

replies.label: You never asked
replies.result: That's fair. I'm asking now.

text: When is {meet}? I took the day off. Don't tell your aunt, she thinks I'm at the dentist.

replies.label: I'm really glad
replies.result: Me too. I should have come before.

replies.label: Now I'm nervous
replies.result: Don't be. I'll be the one in the blue jacket.

text: Your coach's message said 'threshold run'. What does that mean? Is it dangerous?
Why do you run in circles for an hour and call it 'easy'?
What is a PB? Your aunt asked and I didn't know.

replies.label: Let me explain
replies.result: Oh! So that's why you're always hungry.

replies.label: It's complicated
replies.result: Everything is complicated with you two. You and your coach.

text.text: Skiing on Saturday? The tracks at the lake are finally open.
A hike on Saturday? The national park, sandwiches, the whole family.
Ice skating on the lake on Saturday? The ice is thick enough now.

replies.label: Count me in
replies.hint: fun · your legs may feel it
replies.result: Great! I'll pack the cocoa.

replies.label: I have training, sorry
replies.result: Next time then.

text: I saw the light under your door at midnight again. Phone off at ten, please.
You were on your phone until one o'clock. You have a hard session tomorrow, don't you?

replies.label: OK, phone off at ten
replies.rule: Phone off at ten on school nights
replies.result: Thank you. Sleep is training too, your coach says.

replies.label: Just one more video
replies.result: That's what you said yesterday.

text: You're staying in bed today. I've told the school. Do you want soup?
Fever. Bed. No arguments. I'll bring you tea.

replies.label: Thanks, I'll rest
replies.result: Good. Sleep as much as you can.

replies.label: But I'll lose fitness!
replies.result: A few days in bed is better than a few weeks ill.

text: How is the leg? You've been quiet all week.
I know you hate this. Do you want to do something together while you can't run? A film?

replies.label: A film would be nice
replies.result: You choose. No sports films.

replies.label: I just want to run
replies.result: I know. It will pass.

text: I race on Saturday. Come and watch? You can carry my bag, little one.
Saturday, 1500 m. If you come, I'll run faster. Probably.

replies.label: I'll be there
replies.result: Bring snacks.

replies.label: I have my own training
replies.result: Fine. I'll tell you how I won.

text: {pb}, huh. At your age I ran faster. Not for long though, I can see that.
OK, that was fast. Don't let it go to your head. {parent} already told everyone.

replies.label: I'm coming for your PB
replies.result: Ha. Good luck with that.

replies.label: Thanks, really
replies.result: ...You're welcome. Don't make it weird.

text: Before {meet}: don't look at the others in the call room. Look at your shoes. Works for me.
Tip for {meet}: the first 100 always feels easy. It's a trap.

replies.label: Good tip, thanks
replies.result: Free of charge. This time.

replies.label: I know, I know
replies.result: Fine, Mr Know-It-All.

text: Happy birthday! There's cake tonight. And a present that might be shoe-shaped.
Happy birthday, {name}! Who would have believed you'd be this tall. Cake after practice.

replies.label: Thank you!
replies.result: Don't eat all the cake at once.

replies.label: Can my friends come too?
replies.result: Yes, but they go home at ten.

text: Merry Christmas! Sauna at four, then dinner. You're not going running today, are you?
Christmas Eve. The rice porridge is on. If you go for a run, be back before the Christmas peace is declared on TV.

replies.label: Just a short morning run
replies.result: Go, then. The ham waits for no one.

replies.label: No, today is family
replies.result: That's the best present.

text: New Year's Eve! Fireworks at midnight. Are you staying up?
Tonight we melt tin and see your future. Staying up until midnight, athlete?

replies.label: Of course I'm staying up
replies.result: Good. The tin will show a medal shape, I'm sure.

replies.label: I'll watch and go to bed
replies.result: Sensible. Happy new year in advance.

text: Juhannus at the cottage! We leave on Thursday, back on Sunday. Bonfire, sauna, the lake. You're coming?
Midsummer at the cottage again. The whole family. It wouldn't be juhannus without you.

replies.label: I'm coming, I'll run there
replies.result: Great! The gravel road round the lake is 7 km.

replies.label: I'll stay home and train
replies.result: Alone at juhannus? Well, it's your choice.

replies.label: I'll come on Saturday
replies.result: Take the bus, then. We'll pick you up.

text: We've booked the cottage for a week in July. No internet, the lake, Grandpa's boat. A whole week?
The cottage week is in July again. Your cousins are coming. Are you in for the whole week?

replies.label: The whole week!
replies.result: Wonderful. Pack your running shoes, the forest roads are endless.

replies.label: Just the weekend
replies.result: Better than nothing.

replies.label: I need to train at home
replies.result: Your coach will be happy, at least.

text: Cottage week! The water is 21 degrees. The sauna is warm by six. Morning run first?
Morning at the cottage. Fog on the lake. Grandpa is already fishing.

replies.label: Run first, then swim
replies.result: The forest road is soft and quiet. Perfect.

replies.label: Fishing with Grandpa
replies.result: Two perch and a lot of silence. Grandpa's favourite kind of morning.

text: Rippikoulu registration closes this month. Most of your class goes to a summer camp. Which one do you want? June, July, or the day school in town?
The church sent the confirmation school letter. A camp week in June or July, or the day school here in town. Your friends are choosing now.

replies.label: The June camp
replies.result: June it is. Your coach should know.

replies.label: The July camp
replies.result: July, then. After juhannus.

replies.label: The day school in town
replies.result: Fine. Evenings in June, then.

replies.label: I don't want to go
replies.result: It's your decision. Your grandmother will ask, though.

text: Camp starts on Monday. Have you packed? Running shoes too, I suppose.
Your camp bag is in the hall. A week without you. The house will be quiet.

replies.label: Packed and ready
replies.result: Call us. Or at least text.

replies.label: A bit nervous
replies.result: Everyone is. You'll come back with friends for life.

text: Your confirmation party is on Saturday. Twenty relatives, coffee and cake. Wear the nice shirt.
Rippijuhlat on Saturday! Grandma is making her cake. Your uncle will ask about your running all afternoon.

replies.label: I'll be the perfect host
replies.result: And there may be a few envelopes for you.

replies.label: Can it end before my run?
replies.result: It's your party. Stay until the cake, at least.

text: The joint application opens soon. Have you thought about where you want to go?

text.text: Urheilulukio would make sense. Morning practice, coaching. I wish I'd had that.
A good general lukio first, sport second. That's what we think.

replies.label: A sports lukio
replies.result: Then your grades need to hold this spring.

replies.label: A general lukio here
replies.result: Close to home. Good.

replies.label: I don't know yet
replies.result: Talk to {counsellor}, the study counsellor. That's what they're there for.

text.text: Your report card! Up from last time. We're proud of you, school and sport both.
Better grades than last time. Good. Discipline in one place shows in the other.
The grades went up. Fine. If running helps you study, keep running.

replies.label: I worked hard for it
replies.result: We could see it.

replies.label: The tests were easy
replies.result: Don't be modest.

text: Report card day. About the same as before. Average {avg}. Happy with it?

text.text: Same as last time. Steady. That's fine, as long as it stays there.

replies.label: Yes, it's fine
replies.result: Then so are we.

replies.label: I want better next time
replies.result: We'll help however we can.

text.text: Your grades dropped. Is it the training? We need to talk about this.
Lower grades. A top athlete is good at managing time. Are you?
This is what we were afraid of. Grades down, running up. Something has to change.

replies.label: I'll study more this term
replies.result: Good. We'll check in after the first tests.

replies.label: One bad term, that's all
replies.result: Then show us next time.

replies.label: Running isn't the reason
replies.result: Then what is?

text: Your first report card of the year! Average {avg}. How do you feel about it?

text.text: First report card: {avg}. Not bad for someone who trains six times a week.
{avg}. We expected more, honestly. We'll see how the spring goes.

replies.label: I'm happy with it
replies.result: Good.

replies.label: I can do better
replies.result: We believe you.

text: You got your first choice! Congratulations! We'll have cake. And then we'll need to talk about the practical side.

text.text: Your first choice! I'm so proud. This is where it starts for real.

replies.label: I can't believe it!
replies.result: Believe it. You earned this.

replies.label: Happy, and a bit scared
replies.result: That's normal. We'll figure it out together.

text: Not your first choice, but you have a place. It's a good school. How do you feel?
The results are out. Not the first wish, but a place. Sometimes the second road is the right one.

replies.label: It's OK, really
replies.result: We think so too.

replies.label: I'm disappointed
replies.result: Of course you are. Give it a few days.

text: No place this time. I'm so sorry. We'll look at the other options together tomorrow, OK?

text.text: No place. I told you the grades matter. But we'll find a way. We always do.

replies.label: Thanks for being there
replies.result: Always.

replies.label: It's not fair
replies.result: No, it isn't. Use it.

text: Your turn to vacuum today. And your room looks like a sports shop exploded.
Dishes, laundry, your spikes on the kitchen table. Before or after your session?

text.text: Chore list for today: you vacuum, {sibling} does the dishes. No swapping.

replies.label: I'll do it now
replies.result: Thank you. That was quick.

replies.label: After training, promise
replies.result: I'll hold you to that.

text: What should I cook for a runner? More pasta? Your coach must have a list.
I read that athletes need more protein. Is that true? Should I buy that powder?
You eat like a horse these days. Is that normal?

replies.label: Normal food is fine, just more
replies.result: More, I can do.

replies.label: I'll ask {coach_first}
replies.result: Good. Tell me what they say.

replies.label: Pasta every day!
replies.result: Not every day.

text: Saturday sauna is warm. Come before the water runs out.
Sauna's ready. Then sausages. That's the plan for tonight.

replies.label: Coming!
replies.result: Löyly, a cold shower, the evening news. A proper Saturday.

replies.label: Later, I'm tired
replies.result: The last turn is the coolest one anyway.

text: Grandma called. She read your result in the local paper and cut it out. Call her back?
Grandma wants to know when your next race is. She wants to come and watch, with a thermos.

replies.label: I'll call her now
replies.result: She talked for forty minutes. Mostly happy.

replies.label: I'll send her a picture
replies.result: She'll print it out. You know she will.

text: There's athletics on TV tonight, the big championships. The 800 m final is at nine. Watch it together?
The championships are on. I don't understand half of it, but I'll watch the 800 m with you.

replies.label: Yes! I'll explain everything
replies.result: You explained the bell lap three times. It was worth it.

replies.label: I'll watch on my phone
replies.result: Suit yourself.

text: We could go to Lapland in the winter break. Four days, skiing, the northern lights maybe. Interested?
Ski trip in the winter break? Levi, a cabin, cross-country trails right outside the door.

replies.label: Yes, Lapland!
replies.result: Booked. Bring wool socks.

replies.label: I'd rather train at home
replies.result: Next year, then.

text: The autumn break is coming. Do you want to go to Grandma's in the country for a few days?
Autumn break plans? We thought about a few days at the cottage. Mushrooms and quiet.

replies.label: Sounds nice
replies.result: Good. The forest roads are lovely in October.

replies.label: I'll stay in town
replies.result: OK, your friends will be happy.

text: Summer holiday plan: a week in Tallinn and Pärnu in July. Hotel, beach, old town. You're coming?
We're taking the ferry to Stockholm for a few days in July. Want to come?

replies.label: Yes, I'm coming
replies.result: Pack your running shoes. The beach is good for easy runs.

replies.label: Can we avoid race weekends?
replies.result: Show me your race calendar and we'll pick a week.

replies.label: I'll stay with Grandma
replies.result: If that's what you want.

text: The town has summer job vouchers for 15-year-olds. Two weeks of work, your own money. Want to look for one?
Your cousin got a summer job with the town's voucher. Maybe you could try too? The kiosk at the beach is hiring.

replies.label: Yes, I'll apply
replies.hint: a busy summer · your own money
replies.result: Good. Two weeks in June, mornings only. You can train in the evenings.

replies.label: Summer is for training
replies.result: Your choice. Next year, then.
